stories.title: Largest Private Conservation Project in the US Hits Major Milestone as Free-Roaming Bison Pass 1,000
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Out on the Great Plains, a huge conservation ranch just hit a wonderful milestone: its free-roaming bison herd has grown past 1,000 animals. These bison live much like their wild ancestors did, grazing freely across vast grasslands that are being restored as a result. It's the largest private conservation project of its kind in the country, and this growing herd shows the land and wildlife are genuinely thriving together. A nice reminder that patient, long-term work on the land really can pay off.
stories.why_good: A real, measured population milestone (not a projection) showing a successful, ongoing conservation effort restoring American grasslands and wildlife.

stories.title: Drape Some of This 'Plant Armor' Fabric Over a Strawberry Patch to Triple Yields with Less Pesticides
stories.label: agriculture
stories.summary: Scientists tested a new lightweight fabric called Plant Armor by draping it over strawberry plants in real field trials, and the results were striking. The covered plants produced more than three times as much fruit as uncovered ones, without any harm to the plants. Even better, farmers using it needed noticeably less water and far less pesticide to get that bigger harvest. It's a simple, low-tech fix that could make growing fruit cheaper, cleaner, and more reliable for farmers everywhere.
stories.why_good: A real field-tested innovation that already boosted crop yields while cutting pesticide and water use, with no political angle and no hypothetical hedging.
